title: AI Bottlenecks and Value Capture
proposition: As cognitive capabilities become easier to replicate, growth depends on complementary conditions that expand more slowly. Removing constraints creates value; control of customers, scarce resources, and contracts shapes who retains the returns.
network_intro: There is no permanent hierarchy of chips, models, platforms, applications, and trust. The binding constraint depends on the workflow and the moment.

stages.title: Cognitive costs fall
stages.body: More tasks become feasible and more teams can enter.

stages.title: A complement becomes scarce
stages.body: Demand, reliable delivery, or authorization limits what can be sold.

stages.title: Control shapes returns
stages.body: Substitutes, contracts, and customer access determine bargaining power.

stages.title: Investment changes the constraint
stages.body: Capacity expands, competitors enter, and a new bottleneck can emerge.

feedbacks.title: Concentration
feedbacks.body: Profits finance investment, acquisitions, and customer lock-in, reinforcing control.

feedbacks.title: Diffusion
feedbacks.body: High returns attract supply and substitutes; standards can lower switching costs.

feedback_note: Neither concentration nor diffusion is predetermined. The question is which force dominates under specific conditions.
model_heading: From capability to transactions to profit
model_intro: Use one workflow with fixed quality, deadline, and accountability requirements. All capacities refer to equivalent accepted tasks per month.
assumptions: Illustrative parameters, not market estimates. Price and fixed costs stay constant. Increasing contribution margin represents lower variable cost. Expansion and governance project costs are excluded.
model_limit: A short-run approximation with strictly complementary inputs. Actual transactions may be lower; substitution and queues require a richer model. This is not a production function for the whole economy.
margin_warning: Negative contribution margin: operating at capacity increases losses. A firm may choose to reduce or stop delivery.
capture_heading: Creating value and keeping returns are different

capture_rows.creates: Connect a useful result to a budget and a real workflow
capture_rows.captures: Customer ownership, renewals, channel terms, switching costs
capture_rows.erodes: Platform bundling, price competition, easy migration

capture_rows.creates: Make reliable delivery possible at scale
capture_rows.captures: Scarce capacity, usage rights, financing and supply contracts
capture_rows.erodes: New supply, substitutes, capital costs, stale data

capture_rows.creates: Allow results to enter production with acceptable permissions and responsibility
capture_rows.captures: Enforceable integration, cross-organization adoption, willingness to pay
capture_rows.erodes: Native platform features, open standards, weak independent demand

tests_heading: What would support or weaken the model

tests.title: Agent trust
tests.hypothesis: Authorization and acceptance limit a specific cross-organization workflow.
tests.test: Reduce the friction while holding task quality and demand comparable. Measure paid accepted tasks, review time, and net benefits.
tests.weakens: Approvals get faster but transactions do not grow, or customers will not renew against platform alternatives.

tests.title: Startup viability
tests.hypothesis: Lower entry costs can increase experimentation faster than sustainable businesses.
tests.test: Track a consistent cohort and distinguish customer value, independent viability, investor returns, and social spillovers.
tests.weakens: Do not assume fixed winner slots or use failure percentages without a denominator, observation window, and exit definitions.

tests.title: Value distribution
tests.hypothesis: Lower delivery costs need not increase application profits.
tests.test: Follow prices, upstream fees, human review, retention, and operating margins within the same businesses.
tests.weakens: If returns expand broadly and control of complementary assets fails to explain differences, the distribution argument needs revision.

case_heading: Case study: pension and sovereign capital
case_intro: One application of the distribution question: who owns claims on AI-related cash flows, and how do those returns reach households? This is a case within the model, not its central mechanism.
